questions.q: What can an approval process do that a validation rule cannot?
options: Route a record to a human for a decision
questions.explain: A validation rule only returns true or false from data already on the record. An approval process routes the record to one or more people to actually decide.

questions.q: Which wizard exposes entry criteria, editability, and notification templates as separate, named steps?
questions.explain: Jump Start condenses setup into one step with defaults. The Standard Setup Wizard breaks it into the individual decisions, which is what most real processes need.

questions.q: What happens if you leave Entry Criteria blank on an approval process?
options: The process can never be activated
Only records created today enter the process
Every record of that object enters the process on submit
The process defaults to a single approver automatically
questions.explain: Blank entry criteria means there is no filter: every record a user submits enters the process, whether or not it actually needed approval.

questions.q: By default, who can edit a record while it is locked in an approval process?
options: Any user with Edit access to the object
questions.explain: The default Record Editability Property is Administrators Only. You can loosen it to also allow the currently assigned approver.

questions.q: What appears on a record once its approval process is active and a user wants to start it?
questions.explain: Submit for Approval is the action that locks the record and sends it into the process, notifying the first step's approver.
